# (a "before" segment and an "after" segment) separated by a break point,
# with shaded background bands behind each regime.
#
# Expected DataFrame columns:
#   x_column : datetime-like (or numeric) time axis, e.g. monthly dates
#   y_column : numeric measure plotted on the y-axis, e.g. counts / volume
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

x_column = "x"        # time column (datetime64 recommended)
y_column = "y"        # numeric value column

# Break point that splits the series into the two regimes.
# Set to a concrete value (e.g. pd.Timestamp("2020-03-01")) or leave None
# to split at the midpoint of the data range.
SPLIT_X = None

# Generic text placeholders
TITLE_TEXT = "Chart title"
SUBTITLE_TEXT = "Units / measure description"

# Styling constants (structural, not data-dependent)
PRE_COLOR = "#4d4d4d"
POST_COLOR = "#e8562a"
PRE_BAND = "#e9e9e9"
POST_BAND = "#fdece5"


def _format_value(v):
    """Human-readable tick label for large magnitudes."""
    av = abs(v)
    if av >= 1e9:
        return f"{v/1e9:g} billion"
    if av >= 1e6:
        return f"{v/1e6:g} million"
    if av >= 1e3:
        return f"{v/1e3:g}k"
    return f"{v:g}"


def _y_ticks(series, n=3):
    """Pick a few 'round' tick values spanning the data range."""
    lo, hi = float(np.nanmin(series)), float(np.nanmax(series))
    if not np.isfinite(lo) or not np.isfinite(hi) or hi == lo:
        return [lo], [_format_value(lo)]
    raw_step = (hi - lo) / n
    mag = 10 ** np.floor(np.log10(raw_step))
    step = round(raw_step / mag) * mag

text.content: SELECT level, employee_type, ((AVG(CASE WHEN gender = 'Woman' THEN base_pay END) - AVG(CASE WHEN gender = 'Man' THEN base_pay END)) / AVG(CASE WHEN gender = 'Man' THEN base_pay END)) AS percent_difference, AVG(CASE WHEN gender = 'Woman' THEN base_pay END) AS women_avg_pay, AVG(CASE WHEN gender = 'Man' THEN base_pay END) AS men_avg_pay FROM employee_salaries WHERE company = 'Coinbase' AND year = 2018 GROUP BY level, employee_type HAVING COUNT(CASE WHEN gender = 'Woman' THEN 1 END) >= 3 ORDER BY level ASC, employee_type ASC;

rich_text.plain_text: SELECT level, employee_type, ((AVG(CASE WHEN gender = 'Woman' THEN base_pay END) - AVG(CASE WHEN gender = 'Man' THEN base_pay END)) / AVG(CASE WHEN gender = 'Man' THEN base_pay END)) AS percent_difference, AVG(CASE WHEN gender = 'Woman' THEN base_pay END) AS women_avg_pay, AVG(CASE WHEN gender = 'Man' THEN base_pay END) AS men_avg_pay FROM employee_salaries WHERE company = 'Coinbase' AND year = 2018 GROUP BY level, employee_type HAVING COUNT(CASE WHEN gender = 'Woman' THEN 1 END) >= 3 ORDER BY level ASC, employee_type ASC;
